skills.title: AI Skills
skills.intro: The agent skills I use every day in my agentic development workflow.

items.name: grill-me
items.desc: The agent interviews me relentlessly about a plan or design until every weak spot is out in the open.

items.name: improve-codebase-architecture
items.desc: Scans a codebase for deepening opportunities, shows them as a visual report, then grills me through the one I pick.

items.name: caveman
items.desc: Makes the agent talk like a caveman: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept. Fewer tokens, faster reading.

items.name: caveman-review
items.desc: Code review in one line per finding: where it is, what’s wrong, how to fix it.

items.name: caveman-commit
items.desc: Writes a Conventional Commits message cut down to the intent. I use it after every feature.

items.name: impeccable
items.desc: One skill to design, critique, audit and polish any interface: hierarchy, type, color, motion, accessibility.

items.name: frontend-design
items.desc: Pushes the agent past generic AI-looking UI toward bold, intentional design choices.

items.name: agent-skills
items.desc: Senior-engineer workflows and quality gates for the whole software lifecycle, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more.

bookmarks.title: Bookmarks
bookmarks.intro: Courses, tools and sites worth your time, plus the browser extensions I can’t live without.

feature.title: MySQL for Developers
feature.desc: A complete, professional MySQL course that’s 100% free. Honestly, it should be premium.

sections.title: Learn
sections.desc: Courses and guides that are worth your evenings.

items.title: roadmap.sh
items.desc: Step-by-step roadmaps for every developer role and skill.

items.title: AI Engineering from Scratch
items.desc: Write backprop, a tokenizer, attention and an agent loop by hand before touching a framework.

items.title: Go by Example
items.desc: Learn Go through short, annotated example programs.

items.desc: Beautiful images of code, free and open source.

items.desc: Open-source tools that work right in your browser, no account needed.

items.desc: 43 million books and 98 million papers, all free to read.

items.title: OldMapsOnline
items.desc: Historical maps from libraries around the world, searchable by place.

featured.name: Typpa
featured.desc: My first browser extension: select text on any page, press Alt+K, and type right over it, in the site’s own font. Any article becomes your typing tutor.

items.name: Momentum
items.desc: A calm new tab with focus and to-dos.

items.desc: Blocks ads and pop-ups everywhere.

items.desc: Fills any form with dummy data. A tester’s best friend.
